## The Big Picture: What We Built & How It Works

Today's engineering sprint solved two critical distributed systems challenges: process contention and memory exhaustion during large-scale autonomous agent evaluations. 

In autonomous research arenas, running multiple reasoning agents sequentially creates massive execution latency. When agents share a single memory space or wait in line behind one another, evaluations slow down and cross-turn state leaks can occur. Today, we upgraded the execution harness in `AgentSwarm` to spawn **parallel isolated arenas as independent OS-level subprocesses**. Each arena runs its own dedicated agent simultaneously, completely isolated in memory, while coordinating through a shared, atomic stop switch.

At the same time, we addressed data scale. Previously, parsing multi-gigabyte forensic transaction logs required buffering entire files into memory, which risked hitting runtime limits. We re-engineered the ingestion layer in `substrates.mjs` to **stream-parse multi-GB JSONL records line by line**, dropping peak memory consumption from linear $O(N)$ file size down to constant $O(1)$ stream buffer size.

Finally, we synchronized the `kprsnt.in` site platform and automation workflows with the updated **AI Systems Engineer** architecture, establishing end-to-end telemetry and verification gates across all autonomous agents.

---

### Project: `AgentSwarm`
- **What It Does (In Plain English)**: Upgrades the multi-agent research harness so multiple complex research evaluations run concurrently in isolated process sandboxes without crashing machine memory.
- **The Technical Deep Dive**:
  - Introduced `run-step-parallel.mjs`, which coordinates two isolated arena environments and spawns independent Step 5 evaluation worker processes concurrently.
  - Implemented an atomic `stopPath` mechanism in `engine.mjs`. When an abort or completion condition triggers in any arena, the signal propagates across processes to terminate running workers cleanly without orphaned subprocesses.
  - Re-architected `substrates.mjs` with Node.js stream interfaces (`readline` / transform streams) to ingest multi-gigabyte forensic JSONL logs incrementally, eliminating heap spikes.
  - Documented forensic arena invariants across `arena/corpus-index.mjs`, `arena/audit/annotations.json`, and architecture specs in `arena/docs/stories/`.
- **Why It Matters & Trade-offs Handled**:
  - **Memory Safety**: Streaming large datasets ensures long-running agent benchmarks can process dozens of epochs without memory pressure or garbage collection thrashing.
  - **Subprocess Isolation**: Running agents in separate processes prevents shared-state pollution and guarantees reproducible evaluation runs.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["run-step-parallel.mjs (Coordinator)"] -->|Spawns Subprocess 1| B["Arena 1: Research Agent A"]
    A -->|Spawns Subprocess 2| C["Arena 2: Research Agent B"]
    B -->|Watches Atomic Signal| D["Shared stopPath File"]
    C -->|Watches Atomic Signal| D
    E["substrates.mjs"] -->|Streams O(1) Chunks| F["Multi-GB Forensic JSONL"]
```
